answer_text: - Physical activity: at least 30 minutes of regular activity for at least 5 days a week (150 minutes a week). - Note: the 2023 NP-NCD main text describes the CBAC cut-off as "4 or more", while the CBAC form says "above 4"; this document follows the form. (NCD-3.1).
1st and 3rd trimester: 11.0 or more, 10.0-10.9, 7.0-9.9, below 7.0 Trimester: No anaemia, Mild, Moderate, Severe 2nd trimester: 10.5 or more, 9.5-10.4, 7.0-9.4, below 7.0 (ANC-3.1).

Unconscious Diabetes Patient / Severe Hypoglycemia: Unconscious diabetes patient: REFER IMMEDIATELY; give nothing by mouth. Call 108 for emergency care (ESC-6.3). (ESC-6.3). Refer immediately. (Note: Negation word detected in clinical text; escalating fail-safe per emergency protocol).

- Give frequent small sips from a cup (or spoon). If the child vomits, wait 10 minutes, then continue more slowly. Age: ORS after each loose stool - Continue giving extra fluid until the diarrhoea stops. Give the mother 2 packets of ORS to use at home. (CHD-1.2).

- After delivery: one Red IFA tablet daily for 180 days (up to 6 months after delivery). - One Red IFA tablet daily for 180 days, starting from the second trimester of pregnancy. Each tablet contains 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid. - Do not take IFA and calcium tablets together: take calcium with meals, and IFA at bedtime or at least two hours after a meal. (ANC-2.2).

Child or Newborn Not Able to Drink or Breastfeed: Child is not able to drink or breastfeed: REFER IMMEDIATELY to SNCU / CHC / Hospital. General danger sign. (ESC-5.1). Refer immediately. (Note: Negation word detected in clinical text; escalating fail-safe per emergency protocol).

Severe Headache, Visual Disturbances, or Swelling of the Face (Pre-eclampsia): Swelling of the face with headache or visual disturbance: REFER IMMEDIATELY to FRU/Hospital for pre-eclampsia. Check BP immediately. (ESC-2.3). Refer immediately.
Medicine doses are not in this protocol; ask the ANM/MO (SCP-1.2, CHD-2.3).

- Each tablet: 500 mg elemental calcium + 250 IU vitamin D3. - Twice a day (total 1 g calcium per day), starting from 14 weeks of pregnancy up to 6 months after delivery. - Take with meals, never on an empty stomach. Do not take calcium and IFA tablets together, because calcium reduces iron absorption. (ANC-2.3).
Result: MUAC, Colour on the tape Severe acute malnutrition (SAM): below 11.5 cm, or oedema of both feet at any MUAC, red No acute malnutrition: 12.5 cm or more, green (NUT-1.2).
Not covered; see the Medical Officer (SCP-1.2).

- fIPV-3 (third fractional IPV dose) at 9 months, given together with MR-1 (added to the schedule from 1 January 2023; children who received MR-1 by 31 December 2022 are not called again for fIPV-3). - MR-1 (measles-rubella) at 9 completed months to 12 months; can be given till 5 years of age. - Vitamin A 1st dose (1 lakh IU, 1 ml) at 9 completed months with MR-1. (IMM-2.3).
Vaccine: Minimum gap between doses fIPV: 8 weeks MR-1 to MR-2 (if delayed): 4 weeks (IMM-2.6).
- Oedema check: press gently on the top of both feet; if a dent (pit) remains in both feet, the child has bilateral pitting oedema. (NUT-1.1).

- Do not bathe the baby for the first 48 hours. Do not bathe a low birth weight baby until its weight is 2000 g; clean with a soft, warm, wet cloth instead. - If the baby's temperature is below 97 °F, warm the baby by skin-to-skin contact and check again after about 1 hour; if it is still below 97 °F, refer. A baby who is cold to touch, or whose temperature is below 95.9 °F (35.5 °C), is in danger

- grace_days: a vaccine, Td dose, MUAC check or NCD follow-up is overdue when today is more than 28 days after its due date (four weekly session cycles missed). On day 28 after the due date it is still due_today. 4th: Between 36 weeks and term Every pregnant woman should have at least four ANC check-ups. This is only a minimum; more visits may be needed. 1st: Within 12 weeks (as soon as pregnancy is suspected) (ANC-1.2).
Fever Every Day for More Than 7 Days: Fever every day for more than 7 days: REFER IMMEDIATELY for assessment to Medical Officer / Hospital (ESC-5.4). (ESC-5.4). Refer immediately.

Under Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA), a check-up by a doctor/specialist is held at government health facilities on the 9th of every month, for women in the second or third trimester. Mobilise every pregnant woman in the second or third trimester to attend at least one PMSMA check-up. High-risk pregnancies found there are tracked. (ANC-1.3).

- Penta and RVV can be given till one year of age. fIPV-1 and fIPV-2 are also given only up to 1 year. If a child over 1 year still has missing Penta or RVV doses, inform the ANM/MO, who decides the catch-up. - PCV is not started after 1 year. If the child received at least one PCV dose before the first birthday, the remaining PCV doses are completed as early as possible, at least 2 months apart,

- Diagnosis is made by the MO: fasting 126 mg/dl or more, or 2-hour post-meal 200 mg/dl or more, or HbA1c 6.5% or more, or random 200 mg/dl or more with symptoms of diabetes. - A random blood sugar by glucostrip of 140 mg/dl or more is a suspected diabetes case → refer to the Medical Officer for confirmation. (NCD-1.3).
App/login problems are not covered; contact the block data manager (SCP-1.2).
BCG: At birth or as early as possible, till one year of age (IMM-2.1).

- Vitamin A 2nd dose (2 lakh IU, 2 ml) at 16-18 months, then one dose every 6 months up to 5 years of age (9 doses in all). - If fIPV-3 was missed at 9 months, it can be given with MR-2 at 16-23 months of age, keeping at least 8 weeks after fIPV-2. It is not given after 23 completed months (i.e. not after the second birthday). - MR-2, DPT booster-1 (DPT-B1), OPV booster (OPV-B); JE-2 only in endem
Td-1: Early in pregnancy (at registration) Td-2: 4 weeks after Td-1 Td-Booster: If she received 2 TT/Td doses in a pregnancy within the last 3 years - then give only one booster dose (IMM-4.1).

- Chandrapuri is not a JE-endemic district, so JE vaccine is not given here. - MR-2, DPT booster-1 (DPT-B1), OPV booster (OPV-B); JE-2 only in endemic districts. - If fIPV-3 was missed at 9 months, it can be given with MR-2 at 16-23 months of age, keeping at least 8 weeks after fIPV-2. It is not given after 23 completed months (i.e. not after the second birthday). (IMM-2.4).
HIV treatment is not covered; refer to the Medical Officer (SCP-1.2).

- At each visit ask about bleeding (how many pads changed in a day), fever, foul-smelling discharge, pain, breast problems, fits or abnormal talk. Danger signs → refer immediately (ESC-3). - Continue one Red IFA tablet daily for 180 days after delivery and calcium (two tablets a day) up to 6 months after delivery (ANC-2.2, ANC-2.3). (HBNC-3.1).
Lab report interpretation and typhoid are not covered; consult the Medical Officer (SCP-1.2).
Not covered by these protocols; ask the ANM/MO (SCP-1.2).
Convulsions (Fits) During Fever: Convulsions during fever: REFER IMMEDIATELY to CHC / Hospital (ESC-5.1). (ESC-5.1). Refer immediately.

- After a caesarean delivery, visits start from day 7 (because mother and baby stay longer in hospital). Place of delivery: Number of home visits, Visit days Institutional delivery: 6 visits, Days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42 (HBNC-1.1).
Place of delivery: Number of home visits, Visit days Institutional delivery: 6 visits, Days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42 Home delivery: 7 visits, Days 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42 (HBNC-1.1).

Low Birth Weight (< 1.8 kg) or Limp/Unresponsive Baby: Weight less than 1.8 kg: refer immediately to the SNCU (Special Newborn Care Unit). Keep warm skin-to-skin en route. (ESC-4.4). Refer immediately.

Continuous Severe Abdominal Pain or Excessive Vomiting in Pregnancy: Continuous severe abdominal pain or excessive vomiting (unable to take anything by mouth): REFER IMMEDIATELY to FRU/hospital. (ESC-2.6). Refer immediately. (Note: Negation word detected in clinical text; escalating fail-safe per emergency protocol).

2 months up to 12 months: 50 breaths per minute or more Count the child's breaths for one full minute when the child is calm. Fast breathing is: Under 2 months: 60 breaths per minute or more (CHD-3.1).

Under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), pregnant women delivering in government facilities get free: delivery (including caesarean section), drugs, diagnostics, diet and blood; free transport from home to the health institution, between facilities in case of referral, and drop back home after 48 hours of stay. Sick infants up to 1 year also get free treatment and transport. (ANC-5.3).
Severe Pallor with Breathlessness in Pregnancy: Severe pallor with breathlessness in pregnancy: REFER IMMEDIATELY to FRU / District Hospital. Call 108. Do not delay. (ESC-2.5). Refer immediately.

Heavy Bleeding After Delivery (PPH): Heavy bleeding after delivery, a pad soaked in less than 5 minutes: REFER IMMEDIATELY to FRU/District Hospital. Call 108. Massage uterus firmly. (ESC-3.1). Refer immediately.
Baby Cold to Touch (Severe Hypothermia): A baby cold to touch is a danger sign: keep skin-to-skin Kangaroo Mother Care and REFER IMMEDIATELY to SNCU / Hospital. (ESC-4.3). Refer immediately.
